Plot method for pd_adjust objects

Source: R/plot.pd_adjust.R
plot.pd_adjust.Rd

For each hypothesis, draws the range of the posterior probability of the favored (or predicted) direction across the class of priors behind pd.adjust. The left end of each bar is pd.adj, the posterior probability under the prior most skeptical of that direction; the right end is the posterior probability under the prior most favorable to it, \(pd\,\bar{\pi} / (pd\,\bar{\pi} + (1 - pd)(1 - \bar{\pi}))\). The point marks pd, the value under the estimation prior, and the two ends of each range are also printed on the right. A direction is claimed when the whole bar lies at or above the threshold \(c\) (dashed line), that is, when pd.adj \(\ge c\), which is the same as \(pd \ge c^*\). A bar that crosses 0.5 means that the priors in the class disagree on which direction is more probable.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'pd_adjust'
plot(x, labels = rownames(x), xlim = NULL, digits = 3, ...)

Arguments

x

A pd_adjust object returned by pd.adjust.

labels

Character vector of labels for the hypotheses, in the order of the rows of x. Defaults to the row names.

xlim

Range of the x-axis. Defaults to the range of the bars, extended to include \(c\).

digits

Number of digits for the printed ranges. Defaults to 3.

...

Further graphical arguments passed to plot.default.

Value

Invisibly, a data frame with one row per hypothesis and columns lower (equal to pd.adj), pd, upper, and claim.

Examples

set.seed(1)
draws <- MASS::mvrnorm(4000, mu = c(0.4, 0.15, 0.05),
                       Sigma = diag(c(0.12, 0.12, 0.12)^2))
colnames(draws) <- c("b1", "b2", "b3")
res <- pd.adjust(draws = draws, pi.max = 0.8)
plot(res)
